What this is

AI Estate Inventory

An AI Estate Inventory finds every AI system your organization uses across its estate, meaning all the systems you run, buy or subscribe to. That includes model features built into purchased software and tools adopted without approval. Each system is classified by owner, purpose, data class, decision impact and autonomy level. It is the first artifact every AI governance framework assumes you already hold.

Questions We Are Asked

How long does an AI Estate Inventory take?
Three to five weeks for a typical enterprise estate. The variable is access, not analysis. Where procurement records, SaaS administration, and egress logs are available in the first week, the engagement runs at the short end. Where access has to be requested system by system, it runs at the long end.
What counts as an AI system for the inventory?
Any system where a model contributes to an output that a person or a process relies on. That includes purchased software with model features enabled, internally built models, retrieval and agent applications, and vendor platforms running a model on your data. Rules engines and deterministic automation are recorded separately when they sit in the same decision path.
Do you need access to production systems?
Production access is not needed. The engagement runs on configuration, logs, records and interviews. We read only: nothing is deployed into your environment, and no production credentials are required.
How is this different from a software asset inventory?
A software asset inventory answers what you bought. An AI Estate Inventory answers what decides. The classification is built around decision impact, data class, and autonomy, which is what a governance framework and a supervisor actually ask about.
What happens after the inventory?
Most organizations move to one of two places: an Assurance Review, which tests the controls around the highest-ranked systems, or Model Evaluation & Red Team on the single system carrying the most decision weight.
